findings.summary: Declared review baselines game-spec.json and art-direction.json do not exist, so spec compliance cannot be certified
findings.detail: This command reviews against `art-direction.json` and `game-spec.json`, but neither file exists anywhere in the repository (verified by a recursive filename search across all directories including .agents, .corez, artifacts, docs, data and scratch). The only occurrences are prose references inside .agents/skills/game-development and .opencode/agents/*.md. Per the Part 15 requirement that 'every spec requirement in game-spec.json has a corresponding PASS/FAIL entry', a compliance verdict is unverifiable and must not be reported as passing. The review therefore ran against the repository's real normative sources instead: src/index.css (the declared 'Corez Dynamic Monochrome Design System'), PROJECT.md interface contracts, and AGENTS.md architecture rules. This finding is NOT remediated by this pass because only the project owner can author the two specs; every other finding below is recorded against the derived baseline and is traceable to a concrete file and line.
findings.recommendation: Author game-project/design/game-spec.json and game-project/design/art-direction.json (Part 3 and Part 5 schemas). Until they exist, treat this review as a code-quality, performance and visual-contract audit rather than a spec-compliance certification, and re-run Part 15 §1C once the specs land.

findings.summary: Light theme --text-secondary failed WCAG AA on --code-header-bg (4.03:1)
findings.detail: In the light theme, #6e6e73 measured 4.03:1 against #e5e5e5 (--code-header-bg), below the 4.5:1 WCAG 2.2 AA threshold for normal text. Any secondary text rendered inside a code block header in light mode was sub-threshold. The token also failed against --bg-tertiary at 4.37:1. This is the same defect class the existing CSS comment documents for the earlier #98989d value.
findings.recommendation: Darken --text-secondary until it clears 4.5:1 on every light surface it lands on.
findings.fix: Set --text-secondary: #5f5f66, which measures 5.03:1 on --code-header-bg, 5.46:1 on --bg-tertiary, 5.76:1 on --code-bg and 6.33:1 on white.
findings.evidence: node scripts/ui-visual-audit.mjs -> PASS (0 errors, 0 warnings); ratios independently recomputed from the WCAG relative-luminance formula.

findings.summary: Light theme --text-secondary failed WCAG AA on --bg-tertiary (4.37:1)
findings.detail: The same light-theme token measured 4.37:1 against #eeeeef (--bg-tertiary), below 4.5:1. Recorded separately from AX-001 because it is a distinct surface pairing with a distinct measured value.
findings.recommendation: Darken --text-secondary so every light surface pairing clears 4.5:1.
findings.fix: Resolved by the same #5f5f66 change: 5.46:1 on --bg-tertiary.
findings.evidence: node scripts/ui-visual-audit.mjs -> PASS; ratio independently recomputed as 5.46:1.

findings.summary: Light theme --text-muted failed WCAG AA on --code-header-bg (4.21:1)
findings.detail: #6b6b70 measured 4.21:1 against #e5e5e5 (--code-header-bg), below 4.5:1. Muted text is the most widely used secondary tone in the app, so the affected surface area is large.
findings.recommendation: Darken --text-muted until it clears 4.5:1 on the darkest light surface, while keeping it a step lighter than --text-secondary so it still reads as the quieter tone.
findings.fix: Set --text-muted: #646469, which measures 4.67:1 on --code-header-bg, 5.08:1 on --bg-tertiary, 5.35:1 on --code-bg and 5.88:1 on white, and remains lighter than --text-secondary.
findings.evidence: node scripts/ui-visual-audit.mjs -> PASS; ratios independently recomputed from the WCAG formula.

findings.summary: syntaxCheckJS compiled untrusted model output with the Function constructor
findings.detail: syntaxCheckJS() validated generated JavaScript by calling `new Function(trimmed)` where `trimmed` is arbitrary model output. The body is compiled but never invoked, so this was not a live remote-code-execution path; however it is an explicit checklist violation ('No eval, new Function()'), it hands untrusted source to the JS compiler inside the Worker isolate, and it is redundant: worker/jsSyntax.js in the same codebase already parses inline scripts safely with acorn, which is a declared dependency.
findings.recommendation: Parse with acorn using the same options as worker/jsSyntax.js.
findings.fix: Replaced with acorn `parse(trimmed, { ecmaVersion: 'latest', sourceType: 'script', allowReturnOutsideFunction: true, allowAwaitOutsideFunction: true, allowHashBang: true })`, imported from the already-declared acorn dependency. allowReturnOutsideFunction preserves the original Function-body semantics.
findings.evidence: npm run lint -> exit 0; npm test -> 129 files / 1420 tests passed; tests/response-processor.test.js asserts the accept/reject behaviour of syntaxCheckJS and still passes.

findings.summary: Runtime error message was interpolated into innerHTML in the injected preview scaffold
findings.detail:
The React preview bootstrap rendered a runtime failure with `root.innerHTML = '...

' + err.message + '

...'`. err.message is arbitrary text produced by executing the user's generated application, so if it contained markup it would be re-parsed as HTML. Reachability: the sink executes inside the generated preview document (sandboxed preview iframe / published artifact), not in the Corez app origin, so this is a contained injection rather than a cross-origin compromise.
findings.recommendation: Build the message from DOM nodes and assign textContent so the error string can never be parsed as markup.
findings.fix: Introduced renderPreviewMessage(title, detail) in the injected scaffold, which creates the container, heading and paragraph with createElement and assigns detail via textContent, then root.replaceChildren(box). Both the warning and the runtime-error branch now go through it.
findings.evidence: grep for innerHTML in src/**/*.{js,jsx} returns no matches in previewTransformer.js; npm test -> 129 files / 1420 tests passed.

findings.summary: Global error handler interpolated String(msg || error) into innerHTML
findings.detail: The static-HTML preview scaffold's window.onerror handler wrote the raw error text into the document with innerHTML. Same reachability as SEC-002: the code runs in the artifact's own context, but the message is dynamic and must not be re-parsed as markup.
findings.recommendation: Render the message with createElement + textContent.
findings.fix: Replaced with DOM construction (createElement + setAttribute for styling, textContent for the message) and switched the emptiness guard from reading root.innerHTML to root.hasChildNodes(), removing the last innerHTML reference from this scaffold.
findings.evidence: grep for innerHTML in src/**/*.{js,jsx} returns no matches in previewTransformer.js.

findings.summary: JSX preview scaffold interpolated String(msg || error) into innerHTML
findings.detail: The JSX/Babel preview scaffold carried the same window.onerror innerHTML sink as SEC-003, with the heading text 'Preview Compilation Error'. Identical dynamic-input exposure and identical containment.
findings.recommendation: Render the message with createElement + textContent.
findings.fix: Same DOM-construction replacement as SEC-003, preserving the 'Preview Compilation Error' heading.
findings.evidence: grep for innerHTML in src/**/*.{js,jsx} returns no matches in previewTransformer.js.

findings.summary: QR code SVG was injected with dangerouslySetInnerHTML
findings.detail: The publish dialog injected the generated QR SVG through dangerouslySetInnerHTML. The content was verified NOT to be injectable: generateQrCodeSvg() interpolates only computed numeric coordinates plus the fgColor/bgColor options, which are hard-coded literals (#090a0f / #ffffff) at this call site - the QR payload string is encoded as matrix cells, never emitted as text. The live risk was therefore nil, but this was the last HTML-injection sink in the Corez app origin and it is trivially removable.
findings.recommendation: Render the QR through an fed by a data: URL, so no markup is ever injected.
findings.fix: Added generateQrCodeDataUrl(text, options) to src/utils/qrCode.js and replaced the sink with . An SVG loaded through cannot execute script or event handlers.
findings.evidence: grep for dangerouslySetInnerHTML in src/**/*.{js,jsx} returns no matches; tests/qr-embed-publish.test.js still passes (generateQrCodeSvg remains exported and unchanged).

findings.summary: Expanded preview pane outranked dialogs and the lightbox, inverting the mandated stacking order
findings.detail: .canvas-pane.full-width is position:fixed with inset:0 at z-index 1000, while .modal-overlay and .image-fullscreen-modal sat at z-index 100 and .image-lightbox-modal at 999. Because the expanded pane covers the entire viewport, any overlay ranked below it is fully occluded - the Part 16 critical failure 'z-index layer violation causing occlusion'. SettingsModal (App level) and the image fullscreen viewer both use the 100 layer, so the defect was latent in the declared stack regardless of the exact click path.
findings.code: .canvas-pane.full-width { position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 1000; }  /* vs .modal-overlay { z-index: 100 } and .image-lightbox-modal { z-index: 999 } */
findings.recommendation: Declare a named layer scale whose documented order places overlays, modals and the lightbox above the expanded pane, and move the pane below them.
findings.fix: Declared a 15-step --z-* layer scale in :root documenting the canonical order (background 0 -> content 10-20 -> hud 30-40 -> controls 50 -> dropdown 60 -> pane-fullscreen 70 -> overlay 80-90 -> sidebar-mobile 95 -> modal 100-120 -> lightbox 200) and rewrote all 28 z-index declarations to reference it. The expanded pane now ranks below every overlay/modal/lightbox, and all other relative ordering is byte-for-byte preserved.
findings.evidence: node scripts/ui-zindex-report.mjs -> 0 remaining bare numeric z-index declarations; 28 token-based declarations; npm run lint -> exit 0; npm test -> 129 files / 1420 tests passed.

findings.summary: No declared z-index layer scale; 28 declarations used 15 ad-hoc magic values
findings.detail: Layering was expressed as bare integers across src/index.css with no named scale and no documented order: 1, 2, 3, 10, 20, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 100, 101, 102, 999, 1000. Values 999/1000/101/102 are uncontrolled escalation ('whoever needs to win picks a bigger number'), which is what allowed VL-001 to arise. The visual layering mandate requires an explicit ordered layer map.
findings.code: z-index: 1; z-index: 2; z-index: 3; z-index: 10; z-index: 20; z-index: 40; z-index: 50; z-index: 60; z-index: 70; z-index: 80; z-index: 100; z-index: 101; z-index: 102; z-index: 999; z-index: 1000;
findings.recommendation: Declare one ordered set of --z-* custom properties, document the intended order, and reference the tokens instead of literals.
findings.fix: Resolved together with VL-001: the 15-step --z-* scale is declared once in :root with an ordering comment, and all 28 declarations now reference tokens.
findings.evidence: node scripts/ui-zindex-report.mjs -> 'Total declarations: 28, distinct values: 15' all tokenised; node scripts/ui-visual-audit.mjs -> PASS.

findings.summary: document.open()/document.write() used by the injected multi-page router (accepted deviation)
findings.detail: The multi-page router injected into preview and published documents navigates between generated pages by fetching the sibling document and calling document.open(); document.write(html); document.close(). It is an explicit checklist violation, but it is NOT fixed in this pass, deliberately. Reachability analysis: the code runs inside the artifact's own document (the sandboxed preview iframe or the published site), and the HTML written comes from a same-directory fetch whose target is restricted to relative .html links by resolvePageName(). The only party who can influence that HTML already controls the whole artifact, so there is no privilege escalation and no new attack surface. Replacing it requires re-architecting published-site navigation (the surrounding comment documents that same-frame navigation would blank the sandboxed preview), which is a behavioural change with real regression risk that exceeds the security benefit.
findings.recommendation: If a future change makes the written HTML attacker-influenced, replace the write with DOM construction or an explicit navigation. Until then this is recorded as an accepted, documented deviation rather than a fixed finding.

findings.summary: Oversized mixed-concern modules far exceed the file-length guidance (pre-existing structural debt)
findings.detail: worker/index.js is 4,584 lines and src/services/aiService.js is 3,189 lines; src/App.jsx (1,509), src/components/ChatMessage.jsx (1,504) and src/components/CanvasPreview.jsx (1,388) are also far beyond the 400-line guidance and the 600-line 'long-file' anti-pattern. These files mix routing, streaming, persistence and presentation concerns, which is why a review of the request path has to touch a single 4.5k-line module. This is pre-existing structural debt, not a regression, and decomposing it is a multi-day refactor that cannot be responsibly bundled into a review pass.
findings.recommendation: Plan a staged extraction (e.g. worker/index.js route table -> worker/routes/*, aiService streaming/retry/persistence separation) as tracked engineering work with tests covering each extraction.

passes.summary: Emitted game engine uses a fixed-timestep loop with a clamped delta and a spiral-of-death guard
passes.detail: Time.frame() clamps dt to 0.1s (Math.min(((t - this.last) / 1000) || 0, 0.1)), accumulates it against STEP = 1/60 and runs at most 5 simulation steps per frame before rendering - so a tab-resume burst cannot explode physics. A single requestAnimationFrame loop is scheduled, and the frame callback takes its timestamp from the rAF parameter rather than calling Date.now().

passes.summary: Texture/coordinate scaling and object pooling provided; no per-frame allocation in the engine loop
passes.detail: View.resize() sizes the backing store to viewport * min(devicePixelRatio, 2) and beginFrame() applies a single ctx.setTransform, so canvas dimensions match the displayed size. makePool(create, size) pre-allocates reusable objects for bullets and particles, and the frame body performs no object, array or string allocation.

passes.summary: Fullscreen game patch applies a single transform instead of resizing the canvas per frame
passes.detail: The injected FULLSCREEN_GAME_PATCH computes a scale factor once per resize event and applies it as a CSS transform, so the game's internal coordinate system and simulation cost are unchanged by display scaling. The resize/orientationchange handlers are registered outside the render path.

passes.summary: React effect listeners are paired with removeEventListener using the same handler reference
passes.detail: Every window/document listener registered in the audited React components is torn down in the corresponding effect cleanup with the identical named handler reference: App.jsx dragenter/dragleave/dragover/drop/paste/keydown/storage, ChatMessage.jsx mousedown/keydown, ChatInput.jsx mousedown, Sidebar.jsx mousedown, SettingsModal.jsx keydown, CookieConsent.jsx resize/keydown, SecureGamePreview.jsx message, CanvasPreview.jsx message/keydown. No anonymous-inline listener leaks were found.

passes.summary: Audio interval is cleared and the AudioContext is created lazily
passes.detail: Sound.stopMusic() clears this.musicTimer and nulls the handle, and the AudioContext is only constructed on the first user gesture (click/keydown/touchstart), avoiding the autoplay-blocked context leak pattern.

passes.summary: localStorage reads are guarded and type-validated before use
passes.detail: loadPublishRegistry() and loadPublishLineage() wrap reads in try/catch, guard for localStorage availability, and validate the parsed shape (Array.isArray for the registry, non-array object for the lineage) before returning. Corrupt or hostile localStorage content degrades to an empty default instead of throwing.

passes.summary: No API keys, tokens or database credentials present in client-side source
passes.detail: A scan of src/**/*.{js,jsx} for api_key/apikey/secret/password/bearer/sk-/AKIA returned only legitimate identifiers: password form-field state and labels in Login.jsx and AuthContext.jsx, and the privacy policy prose that documents PBKDF2-SHA256 password hashing in legalDocuments.js. No credential material is bundled.

passes.summary: No eval, no Function-constructor use and no client-origin HTML sink remain
passes.detail: After the SEC-001..SEC-005 remediations, a scan of src/**/*.{js,jsx} finds zero occurrences of innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, eval( or new Function(. The only remaining document.write/open is the documented, accepted deviation SEC-006 inside injected artifact code.

passes.summary: All five captured scenes are palette-compliant with the declared monochrome contract
passes.detail: After removing subpixel-anti-aliasing false positives (3x box reduction, 8-neighbour erosion, bounding-box fill-density gate), no solid chromatic region survives in any of the five screenshots: desktop-1440, laptop-1024, tablet-768, phone-390 and thinking-laptop-1024. The brand mark and wordmark are monochrome; the remaining chromatic pixels are text AA fringes confined to glyph edges.

passes.summary: All declared token pairings now pass WCAG AA in both themes
passes.detail: scripts/ui-visual-audit.mjs evaluates every text token against every surface token in both themes (48 pairings). After the AX-001..AX-003 fixes, zero pairings fall below 4.5:1.
